summary: pixel-map-testmetest executes encrypted payload via binding.gyp at npm install
details: The package ships a binding.gyp whose sources entry uses GYP command-expansion `<!(env node index.js...; echo stub.c)` with no native C/C++ source files, causing node-gyp (invoked automatically by npm install) to execute index.js at install time. index.js is wrapped in a ROT-25 Caesar-encoded char-code array passed to eval; the decoded loader AES-128-GCM-decrypts an embedded ciphertext, then reads the sibling data.bin (a 373KB AES-128-GCM encrypted + gzip-compressed blob, sha256 74a728fb7ee7ac6c47263def3f104974a1b7032090c8f9005116526bc742e09c), AES-GCM-decrypts and gunzips it, and executes the resulting code by spawning the Bun runtime (`spawn(bunPath,['run','-'])`) and piping the plaintext into its stdin. The `bun` npm package is declared as a dependency specifically to drop the Bun binary so the decrypted payload runs under an alternate runtime that evades Node-targeted inspection. package.json sets `"stub": true` and the README describes it as a 'Temporary Holding Version', but the shipped artifact contains an encrypted install-time payload rather than placeholder content.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
